parole.significato: a shark, fish of the superorder Selachimorpha (sometimes also including certain extinct shark-like members of the Elasm…
parole.testo: From Middle Dutch haeye, from Old Norse hár (“shark”), with the /j/ appearing influenced by the declined forms /hajə(n)/. Probably from Proto-Germanic *hanh-u-, related to *hakô (“hook”), referring to the shark's back fin. Cognate with Swedish haj, and German Hai.

parole.significato: small body of water, like a pool; gave rise to place names
parole.testo: From Middle Dutch leke, from Old Dutch *leke, from Old Norse lœkr, from Proto-Germanic *lōkiz. Cognate with Dutch laak, English lake.

parole.significato: reef: a chain or range of rocks lying at or near the surface of the water
parole.testo: From Middle Dutch rif, ref, from Old Norse rif (literally “rib”), from Proto-Germanic *ribją.

parole.significato: to eat sweets or other tasty foods
parole.testo: Attested from the 16th century. Etymology unclear, but Philippa et al. posit a derivation from Dutch snappen.
